title: Mali Empire
capsule: The Mali Empire was a Mande-speaking state in West Africa founded by Sundiata Keita, who defeated the Sosso ruler Sumanguru Kante at the Battle of Kirina c. 1235 and established the mansa (emperor) title. Under Mansa Musa (r. 1312–1337) it controlled the trans-Saharan gold and salt trade, commanded an empire stretching from the Atlantic coast to the Niger Bend, and Musa's famous pilgrimage to Mecca in 1324–1325 — during which he distributed so much gold in Cairo that he reportedly depressed the metal's price for a decade — brought Mali to international attention. Songhay pressure from the east and internal succession disputes eroded Mali's power across the fifteenth century; the Songhay Empire had absorbed most of its eastern territories by the early sixteenth century, and residual Mali polities survived in the Mande heartland until approximately 1610.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The territorial extent of the Mali Empire is poorly documented in cartographic terms and is reconstructed primarily from oral tradition, Ibn Battuta's 1352 account, and later Arabic chronicles; boundaries are approximate and disputed in scholarship.
